name: piston_compressor_identification
title: Piston compressor - parameter identification from two operating points
summary: Piston air compressor between 1 bar / 15 C suction and 3-10 bar discharge: four parameters (swept volume, clearance factor, constant electromechanical losses, loss factor) identified from two measured operating points (square system) are imposed at their rounded values, and the model predicts the flow rate and power at two new operating points (10 bar at 3000 rpm, 7 bar at 2500 rpm).

authors: Stéphane Bertagnolio (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory, EES solution)
Vincent Lemort (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory, original exercise)
origin.course: ULiège, Machines et systèmes thermiques, repetition 1, exercise 1

verification.reference: EES stored solution of thermo_models TM-0015 (MSTh-SB-R1-Ex1.EES, EES 7.458, full solution of all 62 variables)
verification.notes: 34/62 stored variables agree within 0.1 %. The rest differ only by the fluid model (EES ideal-gas Air vs CoolProp real Air): absolute h/s carry a constant reference-state offset (+125.87 kJ/kg on h) while energy differences agree (w_s within 0.11 %); identified parameters within 1.0 % (alpha), 0.50 % (C), 0.39 % (W_dot_loss_0), V_s 0.02 %; predictions M_dot_3/W_dot_3/M_dot_4/W_dot_4 within 0.10-0.27 %. No unit conversion needed (SI-C-Pa-J).
